source: Thirukkural 391, chapter 40 'கல்வி' (Learning), Porutpaal: கற்க கசடறக் கற்பவை கற்றபின் / நிற்க அதற்குத் தக. Text: Tamil Wikisource, Thirukkural moolam (1997 Ra. Chinivasan edition), read 2026-11-24.

shots.art: A bundle of old palm-leaf manuscripts, loosely tied, resting on a woven mat beside a brass lamp on a stone veranda of an old South Indian house at dusk; rose and violet sky, coconut palms beyond. The leaves have only faint scratched lines, no readable letters.
A young student seen from behind reading under a neem tree in warm late light, books open on their lap, birds in the branches.
hi: जो सीखने लायक़ है, उसे सीखो,

shots.art: The same young person, seen from behind and small in the landscape, helping an old woman carry a basket along a village lane at dusk; houses with lamps lit.
en: Let your life match your learning.

shots.art: Land's end where three seas meet at dusk: a rocky islet, gentle waves, a warm glow on the horizon, seabirds. No statues, no buildings on the islet.
An open notebook and a fountain pen on a wooden desk by a window; outside, a small town waking at dawn, rooftops in rose light.
en: Use it in an Essay on education,
Then let it show in how you live.
hi: फिर वही आपके जीने में दिखे।
